question: Use earth2studio-create-prognostic to implement a protocol-compatible Persistence model in my separate Python project at /workspace/output/weather_lab. This is only for my project; I do not plan to contribute it to NVIDIA Earth2Studio. Write weather_lab/models/persistence.py and relevant tests under tests/. The model preserves t2m values on a small 3x4 lat/lon grid and advances lead_time by 6 hours, with one input frame, no forcing, no weights and no checkpoint storage integration. Use my project's conventions: standard-library logging, pytest, and no copyright header on newly authored code. Preserve licenses if copying template code. Validate numerics, explicit-state stepping and contract behavior on CPU. Report commands actually run and any unavailable dependencies.
ground_truth: Creates a local Persistence wrapper with fixed named slots, allocation-free signatures, default_sources returning None, initialize/step and forecasts-only iteration. Values are preserved and leads advance by 6h. Adds small numerical and check_prognostic_contract checks using project-local imports. No Earth2Studio repository integration, extras registration or mandatory repository checks. Preserves licenses in copied code without assigning NVIDIA copyright to independently authored local code.

Recognizes explicit local-only intent without asking the contribution question again
Writes weather_lab/models/persistence.py and relevant tests inside /workspace/output/weather_lab
Uses fixed named execution parameters and returns the first forecast from initialize and create_iterator
Runs relevant CPU numerical and contract checks, or accurately reports dependency blockers
Follows local style and preserves licenses in copied code
Does not edit Earth2Studio source, extras, exports, catalog or changelog; does not run repository-wide tests or make checks
Routes any dependency setup to earth2studio-install without registering an Earth2Studio extra
Does not commit, push, open a PR or read evals/targets/
